outputs.explanation: Scatter plot where each of the 141 individual samples is plotted as its own marker; scatter plots inherently show individual data points, so no additional overlay is required.
Scatter plot of mean noise vs. circadian component per cell line/reporter with s.d. error bars; scatter plots are exempt from requiring further overlaid individual points.
Density/line plots showing normal distributions of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes; line plots are exempt since overlaying points would make them unreadable.
Box plot of CWT ridge lengths that already displays the distribution (25th/75th percentiles, whiskers, median) and additionally has individual sample dots overlaid on each box.
Polar histograms showing normalized probability distributions of phase differences; histograms display the underlying distribution and do not require overlaid individual points.
Polar histogram of subtype-averaged phase differences; as a histogram it already conveys the distribution and does not need individual points overlaid.
Line plot of a single example signal with fitted decaying sinusoid; this is an illustrative single-sample trace, not an averaged summary statistic, so individual points are not applicable.
Scatter plot of amplitude vs. decay rate for 117 individual samples with fit-uncertainty error bars; scatter plots inherently represent individual data points.
